questions: Does the game end immediately when S becomes {1,2,...,N} after a move, or is there a check only at the end of the move (so if S becomes full but the player could have chosen a different move that also makes S full, does it matter)?

Is the set S initially empty, meaning it starts as ∅, and the condition 'If S=' likely means 'If S = {1,2,...,N}'? The clarification says 'makes S = {1,2,...,N}', but is the check performed after each operation, and does 'S=' in the prompt literally mean S equals the full set?
When a player subtracts 1 from A_i and adds i to S if i not in S, does the addition to S happen even if A_i becomes zero after subtraction?
Are players allowed to choose an index i where A_i is 1, subtract 1 making it 0, and then later can that index be chosen again (since condition is 1 ≤ A_i)?

Does 'play optimally to win' mean they aim to win if possible, or to maximize their chance under some tie-breaking? In impartial games, optimal usually means force a win if possible, but is there any draw possibility?
Is the turn order always Fennec first, Snuke second, and so on, with no passes allowed?
If multiple indices satisfy 1 ≤ A_i, can a player choose any, and are there any restrictions like must choose smallest available index?
Does the game end exactly when S becomes the full set, and the player who made the move that achieved that wins, even if that move also made some A_i negative (but condition 1 ≤ A_i prevents that)?
